description.short: One of Vietnam's most famous groves of ancient wild tea trees, recognized as an iconic single-terroir within Ha Giang
description.overview: A small yet revered grove of ancient tea trees in Cao Bo commune, where local ethnic families have for centuries harvested leaves from centenarian wild trees.
description.leaf: Large downy buds covered in silver fuzz, dark green mature leaves
description.aroma: Mountain air, honey, wild forest notes
description.taste: Rich, deeply sweet, with wild forest complexity
description.processing: Hand-picking from wild trees → pan fixation → manual rolling → sun or charcoal drying

history.origin: Cao Bo commune in Vi Xuyen district of Ha Giang is famous for its distinct, historically documented ancient tea groves, central to the community's heritage and livelihoods.
history.development: While Ha Giang as a province is broadly known for Shan Tuyet tea, Cao Bo has earned specific recognition among connoisseurs as an elite micro-terroir.
history.modern: Local cooperatives and authorities promote Cao Bo as an independent origin brand with certified organic and ancient-tree provenance.
interestingFacts: Cao Bo illustrates how specific highland villages can distinguish themselves into world-renowned micro-terroirs, similar to specific gushu tea villages in Yunnan.
